title: PostgreSQL pending outbox query and partial index
summary: A bounded PostgreSQL 17 query proves tenant-scoped pending counts through an ordinary reader, then compares baseline and partial-index plans after exact result parity.

use.practicalQuestion: How does a partial index change database work while preserving the exact pending-message count for each tenant-scoped specimen?
use.changedAbility: A reader can reproduce relational count meaning, detect missing predicates, inspect ordinary-role execution, and assess a query-plan observation within its complete cost boundary.
readers: Technical practitioners reviewing relational query correctness and cost
AI collaborators adapting SQL with source-bound semantics and evidence

provenance.description: Adapts the Enterprise V005 pending-count lateral query and V007 partial-index form; owns newly authored synthetic schema, fixtures, independent oracle and disposable PostgreSQL runner. source-coordinate.json binds exact upstream files, license and attribution.
provenance.temporalScope: Source adaptation from Enterprise ae213e7c01262431030a2a8d81129bed090f1376; local PostgreSQL 17.10 observation records its own runtime and executable-source digests.

technicalVeracity.basis: Eleven focused tests pass with the explicit PostgreSQL 17.10 profile: literal count expectations, three SQL predicate perturbations, two denied reader writes, four relational constraint controls, fixed-workload result parity, source/license binding, and owned-cluster recovery tests. The retained ordinary-role plans are observations; exact counts and index meaning define correctness.

execution.runtime: Python >=3.12,<3.13; PostgreSQL major 17 on Linux or macOS; Psycopg 3.3.6

environmentNotes: The caller supplies an existing PostgreSQL 17 installation. The runner allocates a new private Unix-socket cluster and operates only that cluster.
The read role has SELECT on sample tables. Tenant query parameters preserve query scope; signed authorization and row security retain their Enterprise receiver.

One fixed-workload measurement per variant records sampled statistics, visibility preparation, setting units, plan cardinalities, loops and buffers; variable timings remain outside acceptance thresholds.

reviewQuestions: Which relation predicates carry complete tenant-scoped specimen meaning?
Does a zero count survive while an absent tenant remains an empty result?
Which exact results agree before timing, and what work lies outside EXPLAIN execution time?
Which authority and recovery mechanisms belong to the receiving application?
decisionRules: Keep tenant and aggregate predicates together, and preserve every admitted pending state.
Compare variants against literal independent expectations before observing their cost.
Treat plan choice and timing as workload observations; use exact rows and catalog meaning as acceptance.
Retain the owned cluster directory when shutdown requires manual recovery.

instructionYields.instruction: Bind tenant values through the driver, keep predicate meaning explicit, and install a matching partial index under the setup owner.
Perturb tenant, aggregate and state predicates; inspect exact counts, ordinary-role grants, source hashes and all cleanup exits.
Bring the query to a receiver with explicit tenant authorization, migration lock policy, data distribution and complete-path cost evidence.

practice.codeExemplarGranularity: One SQL count and partial index with a minimal relational schema, bounded synthetic fixtures, ordinary reader, owned runtime runner, exact expectations and retained plan observation.
practice.complexityAndAllocation: Repeated scans can inspect O(N*M) rows; keyed partial-index access is approximately O(N log M + P), while complete results and Python parity lists remain O(N). PostgreSQL plans expose actual visits and buffers; index storage, write maintenance, setup and Python allocation retain separate cost boundaries.

boundaries.evidence: Observed PostgreSQL 17.10 semantics, database constraints, parameter binding, ordinary read authority, cleanup controls and one parity-bound query-plan comparison on fixed synthetic data.
boundaries.trust: All domain values are synthetic. Private local socket access shares the invoking OS identity boundary. Exact SHA-256 and Git blobs provide content identity; application authentication remains with the receiver.
boundaries.transfer: Enterprise owns signed tenant context, row security, delivery transitions, leases, replay, Flyway upgrades and restart acceptance. A receiving deployment establishes its migration policy, distribution, write costs and operational authority.

failureModes: A missing relational or state predicate changes exact counts.
A selected runtime differs from PostgreSQL major 17 or the declared workload grows beyond its fixed capacity.
A body or start interruption leaves cleanup responsible for an owned cluster.
A shutdown failure leaves the owned resource available for local recovery.
recoveryMoves: Restore intended semantics and rerun all independent controls before comparison.
Select PostgreSQL 17 and keep workload changes in a reviewed successor.
Attempt owned shutdown and directory release after body and start failures.
Preserve the owned directory and both failure objects; use its local path to inspect and stop the server before removal.
